literal: Gu Bi, Zhang Li, Liu Jie, Qiu Dui, E Qing, Yi Xu, Yi Gui, Zhou Ji, Dou Daitian, Che Yiluo, Wang Luo'er, Che Lutou, Lu Luyuan, Chen Jian, Lai Dagan, Su Shi, Wan Anguo, Zhou Guan, Wei Bo, Lu Zhen, Lu Luoba, Xue Biaozi, Wei Yuan, Murong Baiyao, He Qinu, Guo Tui, Yu Wenfu
idiomatic: Gu Bi, Zhang Li, Liu Jie, Qiu Dui, E Qing, Yi Xu, Yi Gui, Zhou Ji, Dou Daitian, Che Yiluo, Wang Luo'er, Che Lutou, Lu Luyuan, Chen Jian, Lai Dagan, Su Shi, Wan Anguo, Zhou Guan, Wei Bo, Lu Zhen, Lu Luoba, Xue Biaozi, Wei Yuan, Murong Baiyao, He Qinu, Guo Tui, and Yu Wenfu

literal: Biographies 13: Gu Bi, Zhang Li, Liu Jie, Qiu Dui, E Qing, Yi Xu, Yi Gui, Zhou Ji, Dou Daitian, Che Yiluo, Wang Luo'er, Che Lutou, Lu Luyuan, Chen Jian, Lai Dagan, Su Shi, Wan Anguo, Zhou Guan, Wei Bo, Lu Zhen, Lu Luoba, Xue Biaozi, Ziyu, Wei Yuan, Murong Baiyao, He Qinu, Guo Tui, Yu Wenfu
idiomatic: Biographies 13: Gu Bi, Zhang Li, Liu Jie, Qiu Dui, E Qing, Yi Xu, Yi Gui, Zhou Ji, Dou Daitian, Che Yiluo, Wang Luo'er, Che Lutou, Lu Luyuan, Chen Jian, Lai Dagan, Su Shi, Wan Anguo, Zhou Guan, Wei Bo, Lu Zhen, Lu Luoba, Xue Biaozi, Ziyu, Wei Yuan, Murong Baiyao, He Qinu, Guo Tui, Yu Wenfu

literal: Song general Pei Fangming took Chouchi and set up Yang Xuan's younger son Baochi.
idiomatic: The Song general Pei Fangming seized Chouchi and installed Yang Xuan's younger son Baochi.

literal: Thereupon Bi was given the staff of authority and put in command of the Longyou armies to campaign against Chouchi and pacify it.
idiomatic: Bi was then given the staff of authority, took command of the Longyou armies, attacked Chouchi, and pacified it.

literal: Before long the various Di again set up Yang Wende as lord and besieged Chouchi.
idiomatic: Before long the Di clans again made Yang Wende their leader and besieged Chouchi.

literal: Bi attacked and lifted the siege; Wende fled to Hanchuan.
idiomatic: Bi struck, raised the siege, and Wende fled to Hanchuan.

literal: At that time the eastern-route general Pi Baozi, hearing Chouchi's siege was lifted, deliberated returning the army.
idiomatic: Eastern-route general Pi Baozi, hearing the siege on Chouchi was raised, debated withdrawing his army.

literal: Bi sent word saying: "If you withdraw the army, the bandit masses will come again; a later effort will be hard.
idiomatic: Bi sent word: "If you withdraw now, the enemy will return and a later campaign will be harder.

literal: Before autumn and winter are out, the southern bandits will surely come; to await the weary with the rested is the strategy of a hundred victories.
idiomatic: Before autumn and winter are out the southern foe will surely come; to meet the weary with the rested is the strategy of a hundred victories.

literal: " Baozi then stopped.
idiomatic: Baozi held his ground.

literal: Taiwu heard of it and said: "Bi's words are a long-range plan.
idiomatic: When Taiwu heard, he said, "Bi's words are the long view.

literal: In controlling Southern Qin, Bi's stratagems were many.
idiomatic: In holding Southern Qin, Bi's stratagems were many."

literal: Crown Prince Jing took overall charge of the myriad affairs; Bi was summoned as one of the Eastern Palace's four supports, joining Prince of Yidu Mu Shou and the rest in participating in government.
idiomatic: When Crown Prince Jing took overall charge of affairs, Bi was summoned as one of the Eastern Palace's four supports, joining Prince of Yidu Mu Shou and others in government.

literal: He was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He was made director of the masters of writing.

literal: Though Bi's duties were pressing, he never ceased reading.
idiomatic: Though his duties pressed hard, Bi never stopped reading.

literal: Correct, careful, and close-mouthed, he never spoke of inner-palace affairs.
idiomatic: Correct, careful, and close-mouthed, he never spoke of inner-palace affairs.

literal: His fame and merit equaled Zhang Li's, but his integrity did not.
idiomatic: His fame and merit matched Zhang Li's, but not his integrity.

literal: Men of Shanggu submitted a memorial saying the parks and preserves were excessive, the people had no fields to farm, and begging to reduce them by more than half to bestow on the poor.
idiomatic: Men of Shanggu memorialized that the parks and preserves were excessive, the people had no land to farm, and begged to cut them by more than half for the poor.

literal: Bi entered wishing to memorialize but met the emperor playing go with Attendant of the Masters of Writing Liu Shu, with no mind for affairs.
idiomatic: Bi entered to memorialize but found the emperor playing go with Attendant Liu Shu, with no mind for business.

literal: Bi sat in attendance a long while and could not make his report heard.
idiomatic: Bi sat in attendance a long while and could not get a hearing.

literal: He then rose, before the emperor seized Shu's head, dragged him off the couch, struck his ears with his hand and beat his back with his fist, saying: "The court does not govern—it is truly your crime!
idiomatic: He rose, seized Shu's head before the emperor, dragged him off the couch, boxed his ears and beat his back, crying, "The court does not govern—and the fault is yours!

literal: The emperor lost composure, set down the go stones, and said: "Not to hear memorials is truly in my person—what crime has Shu?
idiomatic: The emperor lost composure, set down the stones, and said, "Not hearing memorials is my fault—what crime has Shu?

literal: Release him!
idiomatic: Let him go!

literal: Bi set forth the full circumstances in a report.
idiomatic: Bi laid the full case before him.

literal: The emperor marveled at Bi's public uprightness and approved all he memorialized, granting it to the common people.
idiomatic: The emperor marveled at Bi's blunt integrity, approved all he had urged, and granted the land to the people.

literal: Bi said: "For a minister to vent his will before his lord is not without guilt.
idiomatic: Bi said, "For a minister to vent his will before his lord is not without guilt.

literal: He then went to the Masters of Carts, removed cap and shoes, and impeached himself begging punishment.
idiomatic: He went to the masters of carts, removed cap and shoes, and impeached himself, begging punishment.

literal: The emperor summoned him and said: "Put on cap and shoes.
idiomatic: The emperor summoned him and said, "Put on cap and shoes.

literal: I have heard that in the work of building an altar, one limps yet builds it, yet attends it in full regalia, and the spirits bless it.
idiomatic: I have heard that in building an altar one may limp yet still build it, yet attend it in full regalia—and the spirits bless it.

literal: Then what crime have you?
idiomatic: What crime have you, then?

literal: From now on, whatever profits the altars of state, benefits the realm and eases the people—even if you are overturned and rushed—you shall do it without regard."
idiomatic: From now on, whatever profits the altars of state and eases the people—even in overturn and haste—you shall do it without looking back."

literal: Taiwu held a great review and was about to hunt in Hexi with his officers; Bi remained on guard.
idiomatic: Taiwu held a great review and was about to hunt in Hexi with his officers; Bi remained on guard.

literal: An edict ordered fat horses given to the mounted men, but Bi ordered the weak ones given.
idiomatic: An edict ordered fat horses for the mounted men, but Bi gave them the weak ones.

literal: Taiwu was greatly angered and said: "Pointed-head slave, you dare measure me!
idiomatic: Taiwu flew into a rage and cried, "Pointed-head slave—you dare measure me!

literal: When I return to the capital I will first behead this slave!
idiomatic: When I return to the capital I will behead this fellow first!

literal: Bi's head was pointed; the emperor often called him Brush Head, so people called him Pen Lord.
idiomatic: Bi had a pointed head; the emperor nicknamed him Brush Head, and people called him Pen Lord.

literal: Bi's subordinate officials were terrified, fearing execution.
idiomatic: Bi's staff were terrified they would all be executed.

literal: Bi told them: "I think that in serving one's lord, making the hunt ill-suited to roaming sport is a small fault.
idiomatic: Bi told them, "Serving the throne, giving the emperor poor horses for a hunt is a small fault.

literal: Not preparing against the unexpected and letting barbarian raiders run free is a great fault.
idiomatic: Failing to guard against surprise and letting enemies raid at will is a grave fault.

literal: Now the northern Di are in full flame and the southern foes are not yet destroyed; their crafty intent watches our borders—that is my worry.
idiomatic: The northern tribes blaze with strength and the south is not yet pacified; they watch our frontiers with hungry eyes—that is what troubles me.

literal: Therefore I chose fat horses to stock the army and made distant provision against the unforeseen.
idiomatic: So I kept the strong horses for the army and looked far ahead against the unexpected.

literal: If it profits the state, why should I shun death!
idiomatic: If the realm gains by it, why should I shrink from death?

literal: An enlightened lord may be persuaded by reason; this fault is mine alone.
idiomatic: An enlightened ruler can be reached by reason; the blame is mine alone.

literal: The emperor heard and sighed: "To have a minister like this is the state's treasure!"
idiomatic: Taiwu heard and sighed, "A minister like this is a treasure to the realm!"

literal: He was granted one suit of clothes, two horses, and ten deer.
idiomatic: He received a suit of clothes, two horses, and ten deer.

literal: Later, when the imperial carriage hunted north of the mountains and took several thousand elk and deer, an edict ordered the Masters of Writing to send fifty cart-ox teams to transport them.
idiomatic: Later the emperor hunted north of the mountains and killed thousands of elk; he ordered the secretariat to send fifty ox-carts to haul the game.

literal: The emperor soon told his attendants: "Pen Lord surely will not let me have them; you are not as quick as horses for hauling."
idiomatic: The emperor soon told his escort, "Pen Lord will never let this pass—you are slower than horses for hauling game."

literal: He thereupon returned.
idiomatic: He turned back at once.

literal: After traveling more than a hundred li Bi's memorial arrived, saying: "Now the autumn grain hangs yellow, hemp and beans cover the wilds, pigs and deer steal the crop, birds and geese waste it, and wind and flood also consume it—the loss mounts day and night; I beg compassionate delay so it may be gathered in."
idiomatic: A hundred li on, Bi's memorial arrived: "Autumn grain ripens in the fields, hemp and beans cover the countryside, boar and deer devour the crop, birds waste it, and wind and flood take more still—losses double by the day; grant a stay of mercy so the harvest can be brought in."

literal: The emperor told those at his side: "Pen Lord is indeed as I foresaw; he may be called a pillar of the state."
idiomatic: The emperor told his attendants, "Pen Lord is just as I predicted—a true pillar of the realm."

literal: Earlier, when Yang Nan dang came in, an edict ordered Bi to send all his sons and younger brothers to the capital.
idiomatic: When Yang Nan dang first submitted, an edict ordered Bi to send all his sons and younger brothers to the capital.

literal: Yang Xuan's younger son Wende bribed Bi with thirty jin of gold.
idiomatic: Yang Xuan's son Wende gave Bi thirty jin of gold.

literal: Bi took the gold, kept Wende, yet treated him without courtesy, and Wende fled to Song.
idiomatic: Bi accepted it, detained Wende, treated him roughly, and Wende fled to the Song.

literal: Taiwu, because he was upright and had battle merit, did not add blame or punishment.
idiomatic: Taiwu, weighing his uprightness and battle service, imposed no punishment.

literal: When Taiwu died, the Prince of Wu was established and made Bi Minister of Works.
idiomatic: After Taiwu's death the Prince of Wu took the throne and made Bi minister of works.

literal: When Wencheng ascended, he and Zhang Li both sat in council; their counsel did not accord with the imperial will and both were dismissed.
idiomatic: When Wencheng came to the throne, he and Zhang Li sat in council together; their advice displeased the throne and both were removed.

literal: There were words of resentment and slander; their households reported witchcraft; both suffered execution.
idiomatic: Resentful talk followed; their families were accused of witchcraft; both were executed.

literal: People of the time deemed it unjust.
idiomatic: Contemporaries called it a miscarriage of justice.

literal: Zhang Li was a man of Pingyuan in Yanmen.
idiomatic: Zhang Li was from Pingyuan in Yanmen commandery.

literal: Skilled in accounts, Daowu knew and favored him.
idiomatic: Skilled in accounts, he won Daowu's notice and favor.

literal: Mingyuan valued his loyal uprightness, enfeoffed him Duke of Guangping, and put him in charge of crucial affairs.
idiomatic: Mingyuan prized his loyal candor, made him duke of Guangping, and gave him charge of state secrets.

literal: Taiwu, because of his long service and merit, employed him as a chief counselor and made him Grand Minister of Agriculture.
idiomatic: Taiwu, honoring his long service, used him as a chief counselor and grand minister of agriculture.

literal: In great military and state deliberations Li often took part.
idiomatic: In the weightiest military and civil deliberations Li often took part.

literal: For merit in campaigning against Helian Ding he was advanced to General Who Campaigns North.
idiomatic: For campaigning against Helian Ding he was promoted to general who campaigns north.

literal: With Prince of Le'an Fan and Duke of Jinan Cui Hui he garrisoned Chang'an.
idiomatic: With Prince of Le'an Fan and Duke of Jinan Cui Hui he held Chang'an.

literal: Frugal, fair, and of great repute; on the day he left office his house had no surplus wealth.
idiomatic: He won high repute for frugality and fairness; when he left office his household had no surplus wealth.

literal: When Taiwu campaigned in Liangzhou, the Rouran Wuti seized the moment to invade; Li with Minister of Works Changsun Daosheng repelled him.
idiomatic: While Taiwu campaigned in Liangzhou, Rouran Wuti struck in his absence; Li and Minister of Works Changsun Daosheng beat him back.

literal: When Crown Prince Jing first took overall charge of affairs, Li with Cui Hao and others assisted in government, loyal in serving the throne and speaking only on public business.
idiomatic: When Crown Prince Jing first directed government, Li with Cui Hao and others aided the rule, loyal to the throne and speaking only on state affairs.

literal: An edict granted Hao and Li each a thousand bolts of cloth and silk to reward old merit.
idiomatic: An edict granted Hao and Li each a thousand bolts of cloth and silk in reward for long service.

literal: When the Prince of Wu Yu was established, Li was made Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: When Prince of Wu Yu was enthroned, Li was made grand commandant.

literal: Later, when Wencheng ascended, he was executed together with Gu Bi.
idiomatic: Later, when Wencheng came to the throne, he was executed in the same case as Gu Bi.

literal: Liu Jie, a man of Xindu in Chang Le.
idiomatic: Liu Jie was from Xindu in Chang Le commandery.

literal: In Zhaocheng's time the Murong clan came to present a woman; his grandfather Sheng became household retainer of the princess and followed into Wei.
idiomatic: In Zhaocheng's reign the Murong sent a princess; his grandfather Sheng became a household retainer and followed her into Wei.

literal: He was granted a wife and concubines; a son Ti was born, who reached Administrator of Leling and was enfeoffed Baron of Xindu.
idiomatic: He was given a wife and concubines; a son Ti was born, who rose to administrator of Leling and was enfeoffed baron of Xindu.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: Ti died.

literal: Jie inherited Ti's title.
idiomatic: Jie inherited Ti's title.

literal: He repeatedly followed campaigns with merit and was advanced to Duke of Kuaiji.
idiomatic: He campaigned again and again with merit and was raised to Duke of Kuaiji.

literal: Later he with Marquis of Yong'an Wei Qin and Meritorious General Yuan Qu attacked the rebellious Hu at Tujing and was seized by them and sent to Helian Qubing.
idiomatic: Later he with Wei Qin, Marquis of Yong'an, and Meritorious General Yuan Qu struck the rebel Hu at Tujing; the enemy seized him and sent him to Helian Qubing.

literal: Jie's voice and spirit did not waver; he called Qubing by his style name and spoke with him, his expression calm.
idiomatic: Jie's voice never broke; he called Qubing by his style and spoke freely, his face unchanged.

literal: Qubing admired him and released him.
idiomatic: Qubing admired his spirit and let him go.

literal: Later he returned to the state and oversaw eastern affairs.
idiomatic: Later he returned and oversaw the eastern administration.

literal: When Mingyuan was ill, Taiwu supervised the state; Jie with Gu Bi and others were selected to attend the Eastern Palace and handle critical affairs.
idiomatic: When Mingyuan fell ill and Taiwu oversaw the realm, Jie with Gu Bi and others were chosen to serve the Eastern Palace and handle secrets.

literal: When Taiwu took the throne, he marveled at his pillar-and-timber usefulness and entrusted great responsibility.
idiomatic: At Taiwu's accession the court, seeing a pillar of state in him, gave him heavy trust.

literal: When military and state affairs were discussed, court ministers all praised his ability.
idiomatic: In council on war and state, every minister praised his capacity.

literal: He was thereupon promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing and changed to Duke of Julu.
idiomatic: He was raised to director of the masters of writing and made Duke of Julu.

literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned west, Jie was vanguard.
idiomatic: On the western campaign Jie led the van.

literal: Juqu Mujian's younger brother Donglai resisted south of the city; Jie trusted the diviner's words that the day and hour were inauspicious, beat the drums and withdrew the formation, so Donglai was able to enter the city.
idiomatic: Juqu Mujian's brother Donglai resisted south of the city; Jie trusted a diviner that the day and hour were ill-omened, beat the drums and drew the line back, and Donglai entered the city.

literal: Taiwu was slightly displeased.
idiomatic: Taiwu was somewhat displeased.

literal: Jie had long been in the privy council, relying on favor to act on his own authority; the emperor's heart grew somewhat displeased.
idiomatic: Jie had long held the privy council and leaned on favor; the emperor's heart turned somewhat against him.

literal: When there was discussion of campaigning against the Rouran, Jie said it was better to expand farming and stockpile grain.
idiomatic: When the court debated a Rouran campaign, Jie said they should widen the fields and heap up grain

literal: To await their coming; the ministers all followed his counsel.
idiomatic: and wait for the enemy to come; the ministers all sided with him.

literal: The emperor decided to go; he then followed Cui Hao's counsel.
idiomatic: The emperor resolved to march anyway and followed Cui Hao's advice.

literal: After setting out, he fixed a rendezvous with the generals at Luhun Valley.
idiomatic: Once the army was out, he set a rendezvous with the generals at Luhun Valley.

literal: Jie, resenting that his plan was not used and wishing to thwart the generals, forged an edict changing the date, so the generals did not arrive.
idiomatic: Jie, bitter that his plan was ignored and wanting to thwart the generals, forged an edict and moved the rendezvous, so the generals never came.

literal: At that time the barbarian masses were in great disorder; Crown Prince Jing wished to strike them, but Jie held that it could not be done.
idiomatic: The barbarian hosts were then in turmoil; Crown Prince Jing wanted to strike, but Jie forbade it.

literal: They halted at Luhun Valley six days, yet the generals still did not gather; the bandits had already fled far off; they pursued to Shishui, did not overtake them, and returned.
idiomatic: They waited six days at Luhun Valley, and still the generals did not gather; the enemy had already fled far off; the army chased to Shishui, failed to catch them, and turned back.

literal: The army halted in the desert; provisions were exhausted and many soldiers died.
idiomatic: The army halted in the desert; grain ran out and many soldiers died.

literal: Jie secretly sent men to alarm the army and urged the emperor to abandon the army and return lightly; the emperor did not follow.
idiomatic: Jie secretly had men panic the troops and urged the emperor to abandon the army and ride back lightly; the emperor refused.

literal: Jie, because the campaign had no success, memorialized placing blame on Cui Hao.
idiomatic: Because the campaign had failed, Jie memorialized to lay the blame on Cui Hao.

literal: The emperor said: "The generals were late, and when the bandits came they did not strike—the fault lies with the generals; how could it lie with Hao?
idiomatic: The emperor said, "The generals were late, and when the enemy came they would not strike—the fault is the generals', not Hao's.
